days.title: Wetland Confluences and History
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: río Guadiana
stops.detail: The wetland is formed at the confluence of the Guadiana river and its tributary Cigüela and is one of the most important aquatic ecosystems in the Iberian Peninsula due to the variety and quality of the fauna and flora that inhabit it, as well as for the birds that use it in migratory passages.

stops.name: zona de restauración
stops.detail: The western area of the park —today called the restoration zone— was plowed, drained, and put into cultivation, while heavy machinery moved into the heart of the wetland from the southwest (Guadiana riverbed) and northeast (Gigüela, Guadiana-Azuer), digging deep rectilinear channels in the meandering beds of the rivers.

days.title: Water Sources and Historical Landmarks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Ojos del Guadiana
stops.detail: However, the drying of these humid zones on the banks of these rivers had a disastrous consequence for the entire area: the threat of permanent drying loomed over such characteristic places downstream as the Ojos del Guadiana or the Tablas themselves.

stops.name: río Azuer
stops.detail: In its original and unaltered state, a good part of the water contributions to the Tablas came from the Guadiana river, which was actually the sum of two currents: the waters of the Azuer river (the first tributary of the Guadiana on its left bank) plus those coming from the springs called Ojos del Guadiana, located 14 km from the park in an easterly direction.
